# DECISIONS — Live Work Surface resilience

Scope: ~1.5h, one change, done cleanly. I read LiveWorkSurface.tsx and both
session API routes; I did not touch devcase.ts (db layer looked fine for
what I needed — see #2).

## 1. Loss mode I fixed: close/navigate-away before the next autosave

`flush()` runs on an 8s interval and saves the *entire* current file set to
the session row, not just a diff. So the real gap isn't "we don't save" —
it's the window between a keystroke and the next tick where a closed tab or
a link click away silently drops up to ~8s of typing with zero warning.

Fix: a `dirtyRef` flag, set true on every `onEdit`, cleared only after a
flush's POST actually succeeds. A `beforeunload` listener uses it to trigger
the browser's native "leave site?" prompt, skipped once `status ===
"submitted"` so a normal, successful exit is silent.

**Rejected alternative: shorten `FLUSH_MS` (8000 → e.g. 2000).** Shrinks the
window but doesn't close it, and it's pure request volume for a payload that
resends the whole file set every time. `beforeunload` closes the actual gap
(there's no window where the user can leave without being asked) for one
`useRef` + one `useEffect`. Cheaper and more complete — did that instead.

**Rejected alternative: fix it properly (autosave-to-close with
`navigator.sendBeacon`, no prompt needed).** Better UX, but it's a
zero-guarantee fire-and-forget API and I'd want to verify delivery lands in
the DB before trusting it over an explicit warning. Out of scope for today;
noted for the team.

## 2. Loss mode I saw but did NOT fix: refresh/reopen loses everything

Bigger than the above, and I want to be upfront about it: `files` state
initializes from the `seedFiles` prop every mount, and `sessionIdRef` lives
only in a React ref — nothing is persisted client-side (no localStorage),
and there's no GET endpoint to rehydrate a session's saved files. So a
refresh, or reopening the same apply link in a new tab, discards
*everything* already flushed to the server, even though it's sitting right
there in the DB.

This is arguably the more damaging loss mode, but it's not the cheapest
one — it needs a new GET route, a `sessionId` persisted per-token (e.g.
`localStorage`), and a hydration path on mount that replaces
`seedFiles.map(...)` with the saved files when a live session exists. That's
a real feature, not a small robustness fix, and I'd rather ship one thing
well than two things half-verified in this timebox.

**What I'd do next:** add `GET /api/devcase/session/[id]`, stash `sessionId`
in `localStorage` keyed by `token` on mint, and on mount check for it before
falling back to `seedFiles`. I'd also ask the team whether resuming should
be automatic or require an explicit "resume your session?" prompt — silently
overwriting a candidate's from-scratch restart with stale saved content is
its own kind of surprising.

## 3. Mid-flight update: flaky/offline connections (few-minute drops)

Scoping call, made once, after reading the update: **no new code.**

`flush()` already re-buffers on failure (`pendingRef.current =
batch.concat(pendingRef.current)`) and the interval keeps retrying every
8s indefinitely — no backoff, no cap. That already tolerates a multi-minute
offline stretch *as long as the tab stays open*: the candidate keeps typing,
edits keep landing in `pendingRef`/`filesRef`, and the moment connectivity
returns the very next tick flushes everything. I traced this path instead of
guessing and I'm treating it as already covered, not as something I patched.

What it does *not* cover is offline + tab closed/refreshed during the outage
— but that's the same gap as #2 (no server-side resume), not a new one, and
I'm not opening a second scope item to cover it today. If anything, this
update makes the `beforeunload` warning from #1 more valuable, not less: a
frustrated candidate on dying hotel wifi is exactly who's likely to give up
and close the tab mid-save.

**Rejected alternative: add a visible "offline / retrying" indicator.**
Genuinely useful — not knowing whether your work is landing is its own kind
of unsafe — but it's UI + connection-state plumbing I don't have budget for
here, and it doesn't change what's actually saved, only what's perceived.
Noted for the team, not built.

chat.text: Skim LiveWorkSurface.tsx for me — where does it actually persist edits, and how often? I want the cheapest real gap, not a rewrite.

It buffers events in a ref and POSTs the full file set every 8s (FLUSH_MS) plus on submit. Failed flushes get re-buffered and retried next tick. The gap: nothing saves between keystroke and the next 8s tick, and there is no warning if the tab closes in that window.
Give me a beforeunload guard that only fires when there is actually unsaved content, cleared once a flush succeeds. Minimal diff, no new deps.

Add a dirtyRef set true in onEdit, cleared in flush() on r.ok, and a beforeunload listener gated on dirtyRef + status !== "submitted". That is it — flush() already sends the whole file set each time so clearing on any successful POST is correct.
We just learned a meaningful share of candidates work on flaky connections (hotel/train wifi) — offline periods of a few minutes are common, not an edge case. Whatever you build must tolerate that.
Before I add anything — does the existing flush() failure path already survive a multi-minute offline stretch if the tab stays open, or does it give up after one retry?

It never gives up: on failure it re-prepends the batch to pendingRef and the setInterval keeps calling flush() every 8s indefinitely, no cap or backoff. So a multi-minute outage with the tab open is already tolerated — the risk is only if the tab closes mid-outage, which is the same resume gap you already flagged as out of scope.

notes: Shipped one thing: a beforeunload warning gated on real unsaved state, cleared on a successful flush. Traced (did not patch) the existing retry-on-failure flush loop and confirmed it already tolerates multi-minute offline stretches with the tab open; left the bigger refresh-loses-everything gap explicitly out of scope with a next-step note.
